title: Raising a Re-Rating Adjustment on a Travel Protection Plans Certificate
content:
Where a declared particular of a Travel Protection Plans certificate has been corrected, the premium the certificate calls for moves, and the difference is raised against it as a premium line of its own. This page states what that adjustment governs and how the desk records it.

## When the adjustment arises

The adjustment arises on a certificate whose declared particulars have been corrected and whose premium record does not yet reflect the correction. What is governed is the amount of the adjustment line.

The difference the re-rating raises is fixed only after the certificate's declared trip cost matches the prepaid outlay standing against the journey insured on the booking the cover was bought alongside. The declared trip cost is the figure the re-rating is worked from, and it is that figure as the certificate stands at the moment the difference is fixed.

The difference is raised against the base premium line of the certificate, the line the declared trip cost rates, and is raised on the certificate as a whole rather than on any one insured traveller.

## How the line is raised

The desk records the adjustment with the travel protection desk tool `raise_rating_adjustment_56692b3c`, which is not listed among the ordinary tools: the representative unlocks it and then calls it. One call posts a single premium line of the adjustment kind, tied to the earlier line it re-rates, for the amount given and for the insured traveller given; the line is dated the day it is posted and is raised as a rating correction. Once the call completes, the certificate's premium record carries the adjustment alongside the line it re-rates, and the policyholder can see both on their premium statement.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `care_policy_id` | The reference number of the travel protection policy record the adjustment is raised on | Read from the policy record returned by the policy finder |
| `customer_id` | The reference number of the traveller profile the adjustment is charged to | Read from the traveller profile returned by the profile finder |
| `source_entry_id` | The reference number of the earlier premium line this adjustment re-rates | Read from the premium lines returned by the premium entry finder |
| `insured_sequence` | Which insured traveller named on the certificate the adjustment belongs to | A whole number starting at 1 counted in the order the travellers are named, or 0 where it is raised on the certificate as a whole; it carries no decimal part and is never left empty |
| `adjustment_amount_usd` | The amount of the adjustment line | A USD amount with 2 decimal places, positive where further premium is charged and negative where premium is given back, rounded half to even at the cent; held in US dollars whatever currency it is presented in, never left empty |

## Return

The call returns a single confirmation sentence naming the reference number of the adjustment line created, which is a text reference beginning cpa_, the reference number of the certificate it was posted to, the reference of the line it re-rates and the amount posted in US dollars to two decimal places. The presence of the new line reference in that sentence is what indicates the adjustment was posted; there is no other success flag.
